headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty fell on inflation concerns, but extended weekly gains.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.

why: Sensex and Nifty slipped in the last trading session as inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment.
Domestic equity benchmarks still managed to extend gains for the third straight week supported by foreign fund inflows.
Smallcap stocks and PSU bank shares experienced strong buying momentum during the week.
Easing crude oil prices and global market rotation provided additional support to Indian equities.
whatHappening: HoABL facilitated an early exit for HDFC Capital, returning ₹1,100 crore.
The RBI is open to reviewing the ₹3 lakh annual income threshold for microfinance borrowers.
India and Egypt are working on terms of reference for a potential trade agreement.
Government and private health insurance spending has crossed 20% of India's total health outlay.
summary: On the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices closed lower due to inflation concerns, though markets logged a third consecutive weekly gain. Strong foreign institutional investments, smallcap rallies, and lower crude oil prices supported the broader market trend. The NSE is closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.
